transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05
Start: 10:30 PDT
Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Rina Patel (Aperture Eng Mgr), Carlos Medina (Aperture SRE), Jae Kim (Aperture PM), Samir Desai (Aperture ML)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync focused on throughput tuning. Reviewed last week's runs: warm-cache steady-state throughput, incidents of 429s under burst, GPU util vs batch size tradeoffs. Decided to try a narrower concurrency target and increase batch window slightly to improve token/sec. Agreement to run a 20k-calls synthetic during off-peak and to exchange logs.

Topics:
- Warm vs cold KV cache impact
- Continuous batching window tuning (ms)
- Concurrency target per GPU and global requests in flight
- Queue shaping and priority for low-latency endpoints
- Fallback model behavior during contention

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Rina: Rina here, Carlos, Jae, Samir, all on.
[00:17] Maya: Cool. Real quick agenda: Liam will walk throughput numbers, then we'll go into tuning recs and schedule the spike test.
[00:25] Liam: Hi all. I pulled up the run from Thursday - warm-cache baseline looks like 520 tokens/sec per GPU at our current batch window of 25ms and concurrency 16. p95 around 120ms, p99 spikes to 380ms during bursts. There were about 27 429s total in the 6 hour window, most coinciding with a short burst at 2:14am.
[00:55] Carlos: Those 429s were weird for us. They correlate with a deployment spike but also we see queue depth climb. I suspect request storms from a retry loop in our node pool.
[01:08] Samir: Also worth noting we switched quantization profile mid-run (to int8-ish) which reduced GPU memory but maybe increased per-token compute slightly — can be noisy.
[01:22] Liam: Yep, and the KV cache hit rate for the longest session set was 73% which means some prefix misses causing extra decoder work. We saw that pushing p99 up.
[01:34] Jae: Quick clarifying q: when you say batch window 25ms is that the 'micro batching' window in the Redwood runtime?
[01:40] Liam: Exactly. We call it continuous batching window; by increasing to 35-40ms we can grow batch sizes from median ~6 tokens to ~9 tokens which increases throughput but can add a few ms to p50. It's a tradeoff.
[01:55] Rina: Our SLA for clinical responses is p95 < 200ms. So if p95 climbs above that for our interactive route it's an issue. But for background inference (async analytics) we can accept higher latencies.
[02:10] Maya: Good call. So we need route-level policies: low-latency route stays at stricter concurrency, background route can be tuned for cost-throughput.
[02:22] Carlos: One of our asks was, can Redwood recommend concurrency per GPU for this model family? Right now we used a generic 16 but our GPUs are seeing 72% util not saturating.
[02:33] Liam: Based on the last runs, practical concurrency per GPU for stable p95 is around 12 with batch-window 35ms. At concurrency 12 we still get a ~15% increase in tokens/sec over 25ms/16 in steady-state because larger batches pack better and reduce per-token overhead. The trick is controlling queue head-of-line: if too many requests queue then p99 goes ballistic.
[02:58] Samir: Could a small leaky-bucket token bucket help to smooth bursts?
[03:03] Liam: Yes - Redwood supports shaping by route and can apply rate shaping or token-bucket on ingress. For your case, we recommend burst allowance of 2x for 30s then throttle to sustain. Also a priority queue so interactive requests skip the main batch when flagged.
[03:21] Rina: About model fallback — if the primary model runs out of capacity what's the expected behavior? We prefer graceful degradation to a smaller quantized model rather than 429s.
[03:30] Maya: Agreed. We can configure automatic fallback to a compatible variant — Redwood has model variant routing for that. There's a small perf delta but better UX than errors.
[03:39] Jae: For the synthetic test you suggested, is there a script we should run or Redwood will simulate?
[03:45] Liam: We can provide a script that mimics your production mix — a mixture of 80% background long prompts and 20% short interactive. We'll include sample curl loops and a k6 scenario, whatever you prefer.
[03:56] Carlos: Off-peak window for us is evenings PST; proposal 2026-06-08 23:00-00:30 PDT. We'll confirm.
[04:05] Rina: We'll confirm with infra.
[04:09] Liam: Cool. Now specifics from the telemetry: the batch heatmap shows most batches are 4-8 tokens at 25ms. When we raised to 40ms in a few runs, median batch jumped to 9-12 tokens and token throughput increased ~18% but p95 rose 12ms. The ops delta is acceptable for background.
[04:34] Samir: Did you see any memory pressure when batch size increased? We worry about OOM on some larger sessions.
[04:40] Liam: No OOMs in our runs, memory headroom dropped by ~7%. But with longer sequence lengths the headroom tightens. We recommend a per-session seq-length knob in your client to prevent unexpectedly long sessions multiplying memory.
[04:54] Rina: Regarding 429s, Carlos found spikes in retries. We need to instrument client retry logic to use exponential backoff and jitter.
[05:03] Maya: Action item for Aperture.
[05:06] Carlos: Yep. We'll update the client.
[05:08] Jae: Any quick wins we can try before the big run?
[05:12] Liam: Two quick wins: 1) reduce concurrency target from 16 -> 12 for the primary model, 2) bump batch-window to 35-40ms for the background route. Both are low-risk and reversible.
[05:23] Rina: Do those require redeploys?
[05:26] Liam: No config changes on the Redwood route; just an API update. We'll push a playbook entry and sample terraform snippet.
[05:34] Samir: Also, can we enable 'KV prefix sticky' so sessions that are frequent keep cache warm?
[05:40] Liam: There is a 'prefix pinning' suggestion in the Optimize toolkit; we can enable sticky prefixes for hot sessions which improves cache hit rate and reduces decoding work. We'll include setup steps.
[05:51] Maya: OK let's capture next steps.
[05:54] Rina: Quick question on metrics — when you say p99 jump to 380ms is that for the interactive route or combined?
[06:01] Liam: Combined; interactive-only p99 was ~260ms during the same burst. That's why we need priority routing.
[06:10] Maya: I'll recap then.
[06:13] Maya: Redwood will: send aggregated batching logs and heatmaps from last 48h (Maya), provide a recommended concurrency profile and sample curl/k6 scripts (Liam), and update the pilot playbook to include route-level shaping recommendations. Aperture will: schedule the 20k-calls run on 2026-06-08 and share exact time (Rina), instrument retry backoff (Carlos), and surface any anomalous long sequences (Samir).
[06:42] Carlos: One more thing — for observability, can you increase retention for token-level traces for the next 72 hours? We need to hunt a pattern.
[06:50] Liam: We can bump retention for the pilot to 7 days as an add-on for troubleshooting, I'll include steps.
[06:56] Jae: Pricing question briefly — if we increase retention does that change cost materially in the pilot?
[07:01] Maya: Minor add-on, we'll send a note in the follow-up.
[07:05] Rina: Sounds good.
[07:07] Maya: Any other blockers?
[07:09] Samir: None from ML.
[07:10] Carlos: Nothing else.
[07:12] Maya: Great. We'll wrap. Thanks all.

Recap / Close:
- Tactical: lower concurrency to 12 for primary model; bump batch-window to 35-40ms for background route; enable prefix pinning for hot sessions.
- Test: Aperture to run synthetic 20k call run on 2026-06-08 off-peak and share results.
- Troubleshoot: Redwood to send batch/queue logs + heatmap; Aperture to send VPC flow logs for 429s.
- Fallback policy: configure model-variant fallback rather than hard 429s for capacity events.
